Instruction: Read the segment of a merger agreement and answer the multiple-choice question by choosing the option that best characterizes the agreement.
Question: Is the financial point of view the only factor considered when determining if a proposal is superior, given the company’s fiduciary duties?
Option A: No
Option B: Yes

Merger Agreement: SECTION 8.2. Consideration of Proposals. <omitted> (c) The Company Board may only approve a proposal as a Superior Proposal if it determines in good faith, after consultation with its financial advisors and legal counsel, that failing to accept such proposal would likely result in a breach of its fiduciary duties to the shareholders. The Company Board must consider not only the financial terms but also any potential impacts on shareholder value and company reputation. The Company shall provide written notice to the other party of its intention to accept a Superior Proposal, including details of the financial terms and any relevant non-financial considerations, at least three Business Days prior to taking such action. (Page 45)
